venue: Full pitch width, half pitch length (full pitch for blocks 4 and 5)
theme: Breaking a mid-block: 5v4 on the last line and the switch
focus: In possession against a 4-4-2 mid-block: FB high, W inside, 8 drops on an angle to make 5 on their back 4; the 6 switches play with one open-body action; central 3v2 on their CBs
objectives: Set up 5 attackers on their last line (FB, W, 9, far W, far 8) and two per lane behind
6 receives on the open side and switches in one action (back foot to front foot) to find the 2v1 on the far side
8, 9 and W create a central 3v2 on their 2 CBs and play the pass through the lines
key_messages: "Five on four" - five on their back line
"Open up, switch" - receive on the back foot, play off the front foot
"Make them shuffle" - move the ball until the far side opens
"Three on two" - 8, 9 and W against their centre-backs

blocks.title: Switch rondo: two boxes and a 6

diagram.caption: x2. 4v2 in one end box; after 5 passes, play into the 6 in the middle, who switches to the far box in one action. 2 pressers follow.

blocks.setup: Two 40x15m areas, each split into 3 boxes (14m / 12m / 14m). 8 per area: 3 or 4 in each end box, a 6 in the middle box, 2 pressers. With 3 in an end box it's a 3v2 - make that box the one the switch goes into.
how: 4v2 in the start box: after 5 passes, play into the 6.
6 receives on the open side and switches to the far box in one action (receive left, play right).
The 2 pressers sprint across to the far box; repeat.
Pressers win it: swap with the pair who lost it.
blocks.link_to_theme: Warms up the 6's back-foot-to-front-foot switch and the idea that the far side opens when they shuffle.
coaching_points: 6 opens their body before receiving - shoulders already facing the far box
First touch sets the ball onto the stick for the switch, not a stop then a turn
End-box players make the angle for the 6 so the pass to them isn't straight through a presser
progressions: Add a third presser who can enter the 6 zone
blocks.activity_notes: Two areas running together, 8 per area; pressers rotate every 90 seconds.

blocks.title: Unlock the mid-block: drop, switch, 2v1

diagram.caption: Blue 8 + coach (as a CB) against a red 4-2-2 mid-block. 8 drops on an angle, ball goes 8 to 6, 6 opens up and switches to the far side for the 2v1.

blocks.setup: Half pitch. Blue 8 (CB, 6, 8, LB, LW, 9, RW, RB) with the coach playing the second CB vs red 8 in a 4-2-2 mid-block (back 4, 2 mids, 2 forwards) + GK. Red hold a mid-block: their 2 forwards start level with the top of the circle and only press when blue play backwards. 10 balls with the coach.
how: Walk through at 50%: LB goes high into the winger's lane, LW comes inside, 8 drops on an angle beside the CB (not all the way to full-back).
Count the last line: LB, LW, 9, RW, plus the far 8 or RB pushing on = 5 v their back 4.
Ball goes CB to 8. If their forward steps to the 8, the 8 plays back and the ball moves on to the 6.
6 receives on the open side behind their 2 forwards and switches to the RB/RW for the far-side 2v1 (coach as CB can drop off to give a new angle if their forward follows the 6).
Then 75%, then live. Coach restarts from a CB every rep.
blocks.link_to_theme: The full shape against a mid-block from the video: the 5v4, the dropped 8, and the switch through the 6.
coaching_points: 8 drops at an angle so they face forward on receiving - an open body sees both the FB line and the 6
6 positions behind and between their 2 forwards, ready to receive left and play right in one action
Make them shuffle first: 2-3 passes on one side, then switch - don't switch too early
Far-side RB and RW stay wide and high so the 2v1 is ready when the ball arrives
questions: Their forward followed our 6: who has the ball and who is free?
How many are on their back line? How many are we?
progressions: Red can press when the ball is played backwards
A player replaces the coach as CB
blocks.activity_notes: All 16 outfield involved at once (8v8 plus coach). Swap blue and red at 10 minutes so everyone practises the shape.

blocks.title: 5v4 + GK: central 3v2 to goal

diagram.caption: 8 opens out to the FB, then plays the reverse pass through the lines to the W. 8, 9 and W against 2 CBs = central 3v2.

blocks.setup: Half pitch. Blue 6 (6, 8, LB, LW, 9, RW) vs red back 4 + 2 midfielders + GK. Blue start in the build zone. Red counter into 2 mini goals on the halfway line. 4 spare players: 2 blue, 2 red, swap every 4 minutes.
how: Coach feeds the 6 or the 8 in the build zone.
Goal = 1. Goal from a central 3v2 (8, 9 and W all in the central lanes against their 2 CBs) = 2.
Goal after a switch of play = 2.
Red win it: score in a mini goal within 6 seconds.
blocks.link_to_theme: Uses the 5v4 last line and the central 3v2 to finish, the end product of the whole block.
coaching_points: 8: open out to the FB, then look inside for the reverse pass on the W's back foot
W receives between their FB and CB, and if they can't turn, plays back to the 8 and the ball moves on
9 pins both CBs; the 8 arrives late as the third attacker
If the near side is crowded, play back to the 6 and switch
progressions: Add a third red midfielder (6v7 + GK)
regressions: Red FBs can't leave the wide lanes
blocks.activity_notes: Spare 4 run a 2v2 possession game on the side, swap in every 4 minutes. Coach keeps a ball-stock on the halfway line for instant restarts.

step.space: Narrow the pitch to 45m to make the 3v2 harder to find
step.task: Bonus only counts if the 6 touched the ball in the move

blocks.title: 8v8 + GKs: beat the block

diagram.caption: 8v8 + GKs. The defending team must drop into a mid-block (no pressing in the opposition's 23). Switch of play into a circle entry = 1 point, goal = 2.

blocks.setup: Full pitch, 8v8 + GKs. The team out of possession must set a mid-block: they can't press inside the opposition's 23 (white zones). Spares rotate every 4 minutes.
how: Restarts always from the GK.
Switch of play that leads to a circle entry = 1 point; goal = 2 points; goal from a central 3v2 = 3 points.
Coach freeze once every 4 minutes on the 5v4 picture (30 seconds max).
Last 5 minutes: remove the no-press zones.
blocks.link_to_theme: Rehearses the full plan against a team playing the way a mid-block opponent will on Saturday.
coaching_points: Patience: circulate until their block shuffles, then switch
CB drops off to give their forward a question: follow or protect the centre?
All of Weeks 1-3 still apply - lanes, rotation chain, someone moves, I move
progressions: Defending team can press anywhere (the 'Saturday press')
regressions: Neutral floater for the team in possession
blocks.activity_notes: Everyone plays; ball-stocks behind both goals.

blocks.title: 11v11 (or numbers available): the whole picture
blocks.setup: Full pitch match, normal rules. Swap bibs at 10 minutes.
how: Normal game - no conditions.
Focus: all four principles from the block.
Coach tallies: completed rotations, switches of play, circle entries from a 5v4.
questions: Which principle gave us the most circle entries this month? Which one do we still need?

safety: Shin guards and gum shields for all
Switches are flat slaps or hits along the ground - no raised balls across the pitch in blocks 1-3
reflection_prompts: Could the 6 switch in one action, or did they need a stop-turn-play?
Did we get 5 on their last line? Who was missing?
What do we revisit in the next block?
